# Feature flags (src/lib/flags.ts)
#
# Backed by Vercel Edge Config: a globally-replicated key/value store you can
# edit from the Vercel dashboard or API in place — flags flip for users in
# seconds, with no redeploy.
#
# 1. Create an Edge Config store: https://vercel.com/docs/edge-config/get-started
# 2. Connect it to this project (or paste its connection string below).
# 3. Add an item named "flags" to the store with content like:
#      {
#        "new-dashboard": {
#          "enabled": false,
#          "users": { "1": true, "grace@example.com": true }
#        }
#      }
#
# Left unset, every flag falls back to the FLAG_<KEY> vars below (handy for
# local dev), then to its hardcoded default (off) in src/lib/flags.ts.
EDGE_CONFIG="https://edge-config.vercel.com/ecfg_placeholder?token=placeholder-token"

# Optional local-dev override, used only when Edge Config has no "enabled"
# value for this flag (per-user overrides in Edge Config still win). Handy
# for flipping a flag on your machine without provisioning Edge Config.
# FLAG_NEW_DASHBOARD=true

## What I built

**Backing service: Vercel Edge Config.** It's a globally-replicated key/value store purpose-built for exactly this — reading small config values (flags) on every request with very low latency, editable from the Vercel dashboard/API with changes live in seconds and no redeploy. It's the natural fit here since Notely is already a Next.js/Vercel-shaped app, and it needs no extra service to run (SDK, not a hosted dashboard product), so it stays free and simple.

**`src/lib/flags.ts`** (new) — the flag evaluator:
- Reads one Edge Config item, `flags`, shaped as `{ "<key>": { "enabled": bool, "users": { "<id-or-email>": bool } } }`.
- Resolves a flag as: **per-user override → global `enabled` in Edge Config → local `FLAG_<KEY>` env var (dev convenience) → hardcoded default (off)**.
- 5s in-memory cache per flag doc so a burst of requests doesn't hammer Edge Config; fails safe to defaults if Edge Config is unreachable or unconfigured, so the app works with zero setup.
- `FlagKey` is a typed union (currently just `"new-dashboard"`) — add new flags there.

**`src/lib/users.ts`** — wired in two helpers built on the existing `getUser`/`getCurrentUser`:
- `isFeatureEnabledForUser(userId, flag)`
- `isFeatureEnabledForCurrentUser(flag)`

**`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — gated behind `new-dashboard`; when off, it shows a small explanatory placeholder instead of the team list, still identifying who's signed in.

**`.env.example`** (new, and fixed `.gitignore` so `.env.example` isn't swallowed by the `.env*` ignore rule) — documents `EDGE_CONFIG` with a placeholder connection string, the expected `flags` item JSON shape, and the optional `FLAG_NEW_DASHBOARD` dev override.

Verified: `npm run build` and `eslint` pass, and I ran the dev server both with the flag off (gated message renders) and with `FLAG_NEW_DASHBOARD=true` (full dashboard renders) to confirm the gate actually works end to end.

To turn this on for real: provision an Edge Config store, add the `flags` item with `new-dashboard` overrides for specific users, and set `EDGE_CONFIG` — no redeploy needed after that to flip it per user.
